# HBreadcrumbs

> A wrapping breadcrumb trail with an accessible current page.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This reference describes repository source; package.json version: 0.2.0. Match it to the source/release you are using.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HBreadcrumbs` from `@samishal1998/hearth-ui`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-breadcrumbs>`.
- Individual constructor: `HearthBreadcrumbsElement` from `@samishal1998/hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Layouts.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HBreadcrumbs.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- The last item is the current page and is rendered as text, not a navigation destination.
- Earlier items can be links or navigate(id) buttons. Labels wrap; use short, recognizable hierarchy names.

## Public API

items: NavItem[] · label: string

A `?` marks optional source props. A prop with a default may be omitted even when the source type is required. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    items: NavItem[];
    label?: string;
};
```

### Defaults

```ts
{
  items: () => [],
  label: "Breadcrumb",
}
```

### Events

navigate(id)

```ts
type Emits = {
    navigate: [
        id: string
    ];
};
```

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose arguments as `event.detail`, an array. Listen directly on the element. Native DOM events such as `click` keep their normal payloads.

### Slots

None

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Custom elements do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base, item, current

Use `hearth-breadcrumbs::part(part-name)` for an exposed part, or inherited `--h-*` tokens for system-level styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Supporting types

```ts
export interface NavItem {
    id: string;
    label: string;
    icon?: string;
    href?: string;
    badge?: string | number;
    disabled?: boolean;
}
```

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { HBreadcrumbs } from '@samishal1998/hearth-ui';
import '@samishal1998/hearth-ui/styles.css';
const items = [{ id: 'home', label: 'Workspace', href: '/' }, { id: 'settings', label: 'Settings', href: '/settings' }, { id: 'access', label: 'Access' }];
function navigate(id: string) { /* Integrate your router if using action crumbs. */ }
</script>

<template>
  <HBreadcrumbs :items="items" @navigate="navigate" />
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point (use a `form` instead of `div` when demonstrating field submission):

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

The following is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a stylesheet link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Set array/object properties before connection when they should become reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@samishal1998/hearth-ui/elements';
import '@samishal1998/hearth-ui/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-breadcrumbs');
Object.assign(element, {
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "home",
      "label": "Workspace",
      "href": "/"
    },
    {
      "id": "settings",
      "label": "Settings",
      "href": "/settings"
    },
    {
      "id": "access",
      "label": "Access"
    }
  ]
});
mount.append(element);
```
